title: Why Java interfaces are useful
answer: An interface is useful because it defines a stable contract that callers can depend on while implementations vary. The old claim that an interface cannot contain concrete behavior is no longer accurate: modern interfaces can contain default, static, and private methods. Their central role remains expressing capabilities and enabling polymorphism without forcing classes into one implementation hierarchy.
